lessons: Exactly-once is required; mutate idempotency alone does not satisfy it. This supersedes the earlier 'or state that mutate is idempotent' option. After mutate returns, journal an 'applied' control_decision keyed control/<request_id>.

On consume, if a request_id has an accepted decision plus an applied marker, unlink the file and return without calling mutate or discarding a hold. Call _apply only when the decision is accepted, there is no applied marker, and the lifecycle matches.

Republishing an already-consumed request (the file is gone, so publish succeeds) must not mutate again. Assert mutation.calls == 1 in test_release_is_bound_to_one_never_reused_hold_instance and in any republish test, not only the applied set.

The one window the journal cannot close is a crash after mutate returns but before the applied append. Keep calls == 2 only for that test, and name the window in the test. Every other crash-window test must assert calls == 1.

Keep everything else. Journal-first decisions, stale/conflict/invalid handling, the lifecycle and hold binding, LocalFilesystem.publish, and the DaemonTasks control hook all passed review. Stay inside the six fenced files and leave test_daemon_composition.py unchanged.
reason: A single, concrete, fixable review finding with a clear paved road; it arose because earlier lessons offered idempotency as an alternative, and these lessons now resolve that conflict.
